text:
Glad it's working. Before you rely on it, I got one thing wrong in my earlier walkthrough.

**Correction: Flag C (SUPERSEDED) on identical timestamps.** I said Maya's row 1 would be marked `SUPERSEDED`. It won't. Flag C only marks a row when a *strictly later* submission exists for the same email, and rows 1 and 2 have the same timestamp, so neither gets marked. You'd see two `DUP-email` flags and no indication of which to drop. Use this version in column O, which breaks ties by keeping the lower row:

```
=IF(K2="","",
  IF(SUMPRODUCT(($K$2:$K$421=K2)*
      (($I$2:$I$421>I2)+($I$2:$I$421=I2)*(ROW($I$2:$I$421)>ROW(I2))))>0,
     "SUPERSEDED",""))
```

This keeps the latest submission per email, and for exact timestamp ties keeps the lowest row.

**Related inconsistency:** in Step 6, any `DUP-email` or `DUP-name-time` flag sends the row to `REVIEW`, so even the copy you're keeping gets flagged, and my "auto-resolve exact duplicates" note doesn't actually happen. If you want exact duplicates handled automatically, change the duplicate condition in Step 6 from `M2<>"", N2<>""` to `AND(O2="", OR(M2<>"", N2<>""))`. Then only the surviving copy of a duplicate group gets reviewed, and superseded rows are dropped. Your final filter (`P="OK"` and `O=""`) will then work as intended.

If you hit any odd results, such as date parsing on the `03-Mar-2021` rows or park variants that don't map, paste a few examples and I'll adjust the formulas.
